svg.title: P022 · Orders with more than eight line items
svg.desc: One row per order containing more than eight lines. Order 10 groups lines 1–9. Product 1 repeats on lines 1 and 9: nine lines, eight distinct products, nine units. Order 10 qualifies with nine lines. Order 11 has one line and drops out. Exactly eight would miss the strict cutoff. FROM OrderDetails · one table is enough. Each record is one packing line and includes OrderID, ProductID and Quantity. Those fields supply the line count, distinct-product count and units for each order.
svg.text: Orders with more than eight line items
One row per order containing more than eight lines.
Order 10 has only eight distinct products. Can it still have more than eight lines?
A triangle marks an example to follow. Shaded columns show what to read. SQL excerpts use … for omitted clauses.
Which count defines a packing line?

g.aria-label: FROM OrderDetails · one table is enough
g.text: FROM OrderDetails · one table is enough
Each record is one packing line and includes OrderID, ProductID and Quantity. Those fields supply the line count,
distinct-product count and units for each order.

svg.text: Order 10 groups lines 1–9. Product 1 repeats on lines 1 and 9: nine lines, eight distinct products, nine units.
GROUP BY OrderID / COUNT(OrderID), COUNT(DISTINCT ProductID), SUM(Quantity)
Order 10 qualifies with nine lines. Order 11 has one line and drops out. Exactly eight would miss the strict cutoff.
